page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.m1 server family. It is built on the x86_64 CPU architecture and runs on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 8 vCPUs mapped directly to 8 physical cores with a single thread per core, providing dedicated CPU allocation without hyperthreading. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core.

This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware, requiring external block storage for operating system and application data. Additionally, advanced CPU instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-accelerated cryptography (AES, SHA) are not exposed to the guest environment. The absence of these vector and matrix extensions limits its efficiency for specialized machine learning, heavy cryptography, or vector-intensive mathematical computations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.m1.xlarge offers a predictable resource profile due to its dedicated CPU allocation and standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It is designed for workloads that require stable, non-burstable CPU performance without the premium cost of specialized compute, memory, or storage-optimized hardware. Appropriate workloads for this configuration include standard web serving, application servers, mid-sized databases, and general-purpose enterprise applications that do not rely on modern vector instruction sets.
